lines.text: Why is the gallon of milk or loaf of bread always placed at the furthest back corner of the grocery store?
It is not an accident; it is a calculated psychological trap designed by retail architects.
Milk and eggs are the most frequently purchased staples in American households.
To grab that one carton of milk, you are forced to walk past dozens of brightly packaged impulse items.
Endcaps, bakery aromas, and eye-level snack displays lure you into tossing items into your cart.
Retail studies show over sixty percent of items in a typical grocery cart were completely unplanned purchases.
To save money, write a strict grocery list and stick to it without looking at the side displays.
